places.name: River Park North
places.operator: City of Greenville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 1000 Mumford Road, Greenville, NC 27834. Use the staffed park entrance for the nature center, five ponds, fishing piers, boat rentals, trails, fossil pit, shelters, playground, campsites, and Tar River access.
places.summary: River Park North is a 324-acre nature park with five ponds, fishing piers and rental boats, hiking trails, a science and nature center, fossil pit, wildlife platform, playground, shelters, sand volleyball, group and primitive camping, and access toward the Tar River.
places.hours: Seasonal park hours include 6 a.m.-8 p.m. May-August and 7 a.m.-7 p.m. September-October. Winter and spring hours, nature-center access, rentals, boating, programs, and camping differ; confirm current hours before travel.
places.cost: General park and trail access are free. Boat launch and rentals, camping, shelter use, programs, and some organized activities charge separate resident and nonresident fees; fishing also requires applicable licenses.
places.parking: Use the main entrance at 1000 Mumford Road and follow internal signs for the nature center, ponds, shelters, camping, or trail access. Programs, rentals, and popular fishing periods can increase demand.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are listed among park amenities and are available near developed facilities during operating conditions. Primitive riverside campers must follow separate sanitation requirements.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, the nature center, fishing piers, wildlife platform, shelters, playground, and some paths provide accessible options, while natural trails, boat transfers, campsites, and shoreline terrain vary.
places.trail: Natural walking trails connect ponds, woods, observation areas, campsites, and river access. Primitive riverside sites can require a roughly 1.2-mile hike or boat approach, so select a route before starting.
places.family: The nature center, playground, fossil pit, wildlife viewing, fishing piers, trails, pedal boats, shelters, and programs support family visits. Rental schedules and age or supervision rules vary by activity.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled in allowed outdoor areas, remove waste, and follow posted restrictions around the nature center, playground, wildlife, fishing piers, rental boats, campsites, and programs.
places.picnic: Two reservable shelters with grills and about 40 picnic tables support meals and groups. Reserve for guaranteed use and confirm the shelter nearest your planned pond or activity.
places.landmarks: Key areas include the Walter L. Stasavich Science and Nature Center, five ponds and two piers, fossil pit, wildlife platform, playground, shelters, camping platform and drive-up sites, trails, and Tar River approach.
places.closures: Seasonal hours, high water, storms, trail conditions, fishing and boating rules, maintenance, programs, and rental availability can affect areas independently. Call 252-329-4560 before a specialized or overnight visit.

places.name: Wildwood Park
places.operator: City of Greenville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 3450 Blue Heron Drive, Greenville, NC 27834. Use the paved main entrance for the welcome center, playground, east-lake loop, boardwalk, sandy beach, kayak launch, shelter, camping platform, pump track, skills course, and mountain-bike trails.
places.summary: Wildwood Park is a 364-acre outdoor destination with two lakes, natural trails, a 1.7-mile accessible boardwalk loop, six miles of mountain-bike trails, pump track and bicycle skills course, playground, welcome center, sandy Tar River beach, kayak launch, floating dock, shelter, and camping platform.
places.hours: The park is open daily from sunrise to sunset. Welcome-center restrooms, watercraft rentals, shelter events, camping, organized programs, and after-hours registered activities use separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, trails, boardwalk, beach access, pump track, and bike-skills areas are free. Watercraft rentals, programs, shelter reservations, camping, and events charge separately.
places.parking: The main 3450 Blue Heron Drive entrance serves the welcome center and core east-side amenities. Additional parking near the bicycle facilities may operate separately; use the current park map for your exact activity.
places.restroom: Permanent restrooms are available at the welcome center during operating conditions. Do not assume facilities are available on remote west-side trails, at every lake edge, or after the center closes.
places.accessibility: The welcome center, playground area, accessible boardwalk, pedestrian bridge, floating dock approach, and developed core provide accessible options. Natural and mountain-bike trails, sand, camping transfers, and changing shoreline conditions vary.
places.trail: The east lake has an approximately 1.7-mile boardwalk and trail loop; the west side adds several natural-surface miles, and the Chris Smith network provides six miles of single-track mountain-bike trail with multiple skill levels.
places.family: Families can combine the playground, welcome center, short lake loop, boardwalk, beach, pump track, Strider course, picnic shelter, and nature programs. Match bike features and water activities to ability and supervision.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled in allowed areas, remove waste, and protect wildlife. Follow restrictions around the playground, welcome center, beach, docks, rental craft, bike features, events, and camping platform.
places.picnic: An event shelter is reservable with a two-hour minimum, while ordinary visits can use designated seating and picnic areas. Confirm event schedules because shelter use can be exclusive.
places.landmarks: Look for the welcome center and playground, east-lake boardwalk loop, pedestrian bridge, sandy Tar River beach, kayak launch and floating dock, camping platform, pump track, skills course, Strider area, and Chris Smith trails.
places.closures: High water, storms, wet natural trails, bike-trail protection, construction, maintenance, programs, races, and private shelter events can affect individual areas. Check current City notices before boating or mountain biking.

places.name: Greenville Town Common
places.operator: City of Greenville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 105 East First Street, Greenville, NC 27834. This central riverfront entrance serves the inclusive playground, Greenville Toyota Amphitheater, Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza, Town Creek Bridge, esplanade, fishing and boat access, and greenway connections.
places.summary: Greenville Town Common is a 21-acre central Tar River park with an inclusive playground, Greenville Toyota Amphitheater, Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza, Town Creek Bridge, 1,500-foot riverfront esplanade, fishing and boat access, picnic areas, restrooms, and connections to Greenville's greenways.
places.hours: Use the outdoor park according to posted public hours and riverfront conditions. The amphitheater, restrooms, boat access, rentals, festivals, concerts, and holiday events use separate schedules and can change ordinary access.
places.cost: General park, playground, esplanade, and greenway access are free. Reserved events, concessions, programs, boating services, and special activities may charge separately.
places.parking: Use legal downtown parking near 105 East First Street and choose an approach for the playground, amphitheater, Gateway Plaza, boat access, or greenway. Major events can close streets and redirect parking.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are listed among Town Common amenities during operating conditions. Event layouts, maintenance, and seasonal operations can alter the closest available facility.
places.accessibility: Paved riverfront walks, the inclusive playground, plaza, amphitheater approaches, bridge, and developed downtown access provide accessible options, while docks, river levels, event barriers, and temporary routes vary.
places.trail: Paved paths include a 1,500-foot Tar River esplanade and links across Town Creek Bridge into the wider greenway system. Choose South Tar River or eastbound Green Mill Run connections before leaving the central park.
places.family: The inclusive playground, open lawn, river views, sundial, bridge, picnics, concerts, and festivals support family visits. Check event calendars because crowds, sound, vendors, and access controls can transform the park.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled where allowed, remove waste, and follow temporary event restrictions. Avoid playground surfaces, crowded amphitheater zones, fishing activity, and boat ramps.
places.picnic: Picnic tables and a small reservable shelter are available, with broad lawn space for ordinary public use. Large gatherings, tents, vendors, amplified sound, or exclusive use require City approval.
places.landmarks: Major features are Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza, Greenville Toyota Amphitheater, inclusive playground, Town Creek Bridge, 1,500-foot esplanade, Millennium Sundial, Tar River boat access, and greenway junctions.
places.closures: Festivals, concerts, July Fourth activity, street closures, flooding, river conditions, construction, and private reservations can alter parking and access. Check the City calendar before a quiet or through-trail visit.

places.name: South Tar River Greenway
places.operator: City of Greenville Recreation and Parks
places.address: For the central eastern access use Greenville Town Common at 105 East First Street. The South Tar River section runs west through Town Common to the current trailhead marker at Fairfax Avenue, with a planned extension toward Moye Boulevard.
places.summary: South Tar River Greenway is Greenville's westbound paved river corridor from Town Common toward Fairfax Avenue, connecting the downtown esplanade, river views, bridge and park amenities to the City's approximately nine-mile greenway network and a planned Moye Boulevard extension.
places.hours: Use the greenway during daylight and posted connected-park hours. Flooding, construction, river conditions, events, and work on the planned BUILD extension can affect sections.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Downtown parking, events, programs, rentals, and connected attractions may charge separately.
places.parking: Town Common is the most developed central access. Choose legal downtown parking or another signed trailhead for the segment you plan, and do not rely on construction or private lots near the western end.
places.restroom: Town Common provides the most dependable public restroom opportunity during operating conditions. Plan the westbound section as having limited facilities beyond the park.
places.accessibility: The developed route uses paved shared paths, but grades, road crossings, bridge approaches, river flooding, construction detours, and the western trailhead connection can vary.
places.trail: The current South Tar section passes through Town Common and ends at Fairfax Avenue. It is one component of Greenville's roughly nine-mile system; do not confuse planned Moye Boulevard mileage with currently open trail.
places.family: A short Town Common out-and-back pairs the trail with an inclusive playground, restrooms, river views, and picnic space. Supervise children at water edges, crossings, bridges, and around bicycles.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the greenway where posted rules permit. Keep leashes short around cyclists and events, remove waste, and follow Town Common rules.
places.picnic: Use Town Common's designated picnic and lawn areas rather than blocking the shared path. Organized gatherings and commercial activity require approval.
places.landmarks: Key reference points are Town Common, Tar River esplanade, Town Creek Bridge, Sycamore Hill Gateway Plaza, Memorial Drive bridge area, Fairfax Avenue trailhead, and the planned route toward the VA Clinic on Moye Boulevard.
places.closures: Tar River flooding, storms, downtown events, bridge work, utility projects, and BUILD-extension construction can interrupt access. Check current City notices after heavy rain and before relying on a through-route.

places.name: Rankin Lake Park
places.operator: City of Gastonia Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1750 Rankin Lake Road, Gastonia, NC 28052. Use the main park drive for the clubhouse, picnic shelters, lake office, fishing piers, boat dock, playground, disc golf, StoryWalk, paved lake loop, and Highland Rail Trail connector.
places.summary: Rankin Lake Park is a renovated 242-acre public park around an approximately 80-acre former water-supply lake, with a 1.569-mile paved loop, boardwalks, fishing and viewing piers, seasonal boat rentals, 18-hole disc golf, playground, StoryWalk, clubhouse, outdoor classroom, horseshoes, shelters, and greenway access.
places.hours: The park is open daily 7 a.m.-9 p.m. The lake office, boat rentals, fishing permits, clubhouse, shelters, restrooms, and organized activities have separate seasonal and weather-dependent operations.
places.cost: General park, playground, paved loop, boardwalk, StoryWalk, and disc-golf access are free. Daily fishing permits, boat rentals, clubhouse and shelter reservations, and organized events charge separately; anglers 16 and older also need a valid North Carolina fishing license.
places.parking: Use 1750 Rankin Lake Road and follow internal signs for the clubhouse and shelters, lake office and fishing, playground, disc golf, or trail. Large rentals and popular fishing periods can fill the closest areas.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available in the clubhouse and a separate restroom building during operating conditions. The lake office and rental schedule should not be treated as identical to park hours.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, the paved lake loop, clubhouse, shelters, restrooms, fishing and viewing piers, boardwalks, and playground provide accessible options, while disc-golf terrain, boat transfers, and shoreline grades vary.
places.trail: A 1.569-mile paved loop circles the lake and crosses boardwalks over Kaylor Creek and the spillway. A trailhead also connects toward the Highland Rail Trail; disc-golf fairways are separate recreation corridors.
places.family: Families can use the playground, StoryWalk, piers, lake loop, boardwalks, picnics, outdoor classroom, pedal boats, fishing, and disc golf. Verify the lake office before promising boat rentals.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled in allowed areas, remove waste, and keep pets away from playground surfaces, fishing activity, rental boats, clubhouse events, and disc-golf flight paths.
places.picnic: Two corporate lakeside shelters, one large shelter, eight small shelters, and the clubhouse support gatherings. Reserve for guaranteed use and choose the facility nearest your planned lake or play activity.
places.landmarks: Look for the clubhouse, lake office and boat dock, two fishing piers and viewing pier, Kaylor Creek and spillway boardwalks, 1.569-mile loop, playground, StoryWalk, 18-hole disc-golf course, outdoor classroom, and Highland Rail Trail connector.
places.closures: The lake office is currently closed for winter. Boat rentals require acceptable combined air and water temperature and can stop for wind, cold, storms, or other hazards; events, maintenance, and lake conditions can affect other areas.

places.name: Martha Rivers Park
places.operator: City of Gastonia Parks and Recreation
places.address: 1515 Neal Hawkins Road, Gastonia, NC 28056. Follow internal signs for the one-acre castle playground, soccer, baseball and softball complexes, walking loops, shelters, volleyball, concessions, and restrooms.
places.summary: Martha Rivers Park is a 57.95-acre youth-sports and family park with a volunteer-built one-acre wooden castle playground, four lighted soccer fields, three lighted youth baseball fields, a lighted softball field, batting cages, paved walking loops, two shelters, sand volleyball, horseshoes, concessions, and restrooms.
places.hours: The general park is open daily dawn to dusk. Scheduled lighted fields, leagues, tournaments, concessions, shelters, and organized athletics operate independently and may continue under approved schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, walking, and ordinary picnic access are free. Field use, leagues, tournaments, shelter reservations, concessions, and organized activities may charge or require approval.
places.parking: Use 1515 Neal Hawkins Road and choose the internal area closest to the castle playground, soccer complex, or baseball and softball complex. League and tournament periods can create heavy traffic and full lots.
places.restroom: A restroom building serves the park, and the athletic scorers' and concession area includes restrooms during operating conditions. Availability can vary outside scheduled field activity.
places.accessibility: Paved parking and walking loops connect developed sports, playground, shelter, and restroom areas. The castle playground includes ramps and rubberized surfacing, but its multi-level wooden structure and individual play features vary in accessibility.
places.trail: Paved walking paths loop around the baseball fields, playground, and soccer fields, with crossovers that create different distances. Expect active field traffic and event circulation rather than a secluded nature trail.
places.family: The signature castle includes forts, ship and race-car themes, swings, slides, sand digging, ramps, catwalks, climbing, and hiding areas. Pair it with walking, shelters, volleyball, or scheduled youth sports.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed in allowed ordinary park areas, remove waste, and keep pets outside the playground, active fields, dugouts, concession and restroom areas, and crowded tournament circulation.
places.picnic: Two large shelters are reservable in daily sessions, with additional picnic opportunities around the park. Reserve for guaranteed group use and choose a session that aligns with nearby athletics.
places.landmarks: The one-acre Operation Playground castle is the main family landmark. Other key areas are the soccer complex, baseball and softball fields, batting cages, paved loops, two shelters, volleyball and horseshoes, scorers' tower, concession stand, and restrooms.
places.closures: Wet-field decisions, league schedules, tournaments, maintenance, severe weather, and shelter reservations can affect portions independently. Contact the athletics office before relying on field availability.

places.name: Lineberger Park
places.operator: City of Gastonia Parks and Recreation
places.address: 632 East Garrison Boulevard, Gastonia, NC 28054. Use Chestnut Street for the eastern playground, Vietnam War Memorial, shelters, restrooms, and greenway trailhead; use Avon Street for the pool, splash pad, basketball, shelters, and closed miniature-train area.
places.summary: Lineberger Park is Gastonia's historic 18.5-acre central park, split by Avon Creek into eastern and western activity areas with a large playground, paved trails, Vietnam War Memorial, Avon/Catawba Greenway trailhead, pool and lazy river, splash pad, basketball, shelters, gazebo, restrooms, and a currently closed miniature train.
places.hours: The general park is open daily dawn to dusk. Lighted facilities, the summer pool, splash pad, shelters, restrooms, and events operate independently. The miniature train is closed indefinitely.
places.cost: General park, playground, memorial, paved paths, greenway, basketball, and picnic access are free. Summer pool sessions cost $4 per person age one and older; reservations, concessions, and programs may charge separately.
places.parking: Choose the correct side of Avon Creek. Chestnut Street parking is best for the playground, memorial, eastern shelters, restroom, and greenway; Avon Street parking is best for the pool, splash pad, basketball, and western shelters.
places.restroom: A restroom and water-fountain building serves the eastern node. The pool house has showers, changing space, restrooms, and concessions during pool operations; the western ticket-booth building also includes restrooms subject to operating conditions.
places.accessibility: Paved paths connect parking, the memorial, playground, shelters, restrooms, and greenway. The pool has zero-depth entry, while creek crossings, older park grades, individual play features, and event routes vary.
places.trail: Paved walking paths circle park features and connect to the Avon/Catawba Creeks Greenway. The creek divides the park, so use the bridge and correct parking node rather than assuming every facility is adjacent.
places.family: The playground, picnic areas, pool with lazy river and slide, splash pad, basketball, memorial loop, and greenway support varied visits. The miniature train should not be promised because it is closed indefinitely.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled in allowed areas, remove waste, and keep pets outside playground and aquatic surfaces, buildings, crowded shelters, and active courts.
places.picnic: Each side has a large shelter and smaller shelters, plus a gazebo on the eastern side. Reserve for guaranteed group use and select the side nearest your main activity.
places.landmarks: Important orientation points are the Chestnut Street playground and greenway node, Gaston County Vietnam War Memorial, Avon Creek bridge, Avon Street aquatic and basketball node, pool and lazy river, splash pad, shelters, gazebo, and closed train area.
places.closures: The miniature train is closed indefinitely. The splash pad is currently closed under drought-related water restrictions; pool operation is seasonal and session-based. Construction, events, weather, and greenway work may affect other access.

places.name: Avon and Catawba Creek Greenway
places.operator: City of Gastonia Parks and Recreation
places.address: Use Lineberger Park at 632 East Garrison Boulevard for a developed central trailhead with parking and restrooms. The connected corridor runs along Avon and Catawba creeks toward Ferguson Park and the Robinwood Road area.
places.summary: Avon and Catawba Creeks Greenway is Gastonia's first and most-used paved greenway corridor, connecting Lineberger Park and its civic-area trailhead with Ferguson Park and the Robinwood Road section along creek scenery, lawns, neighborhood links, and the regional Carolina Thread Trail network.
places.hours: Use the greenway during daylight and posted connected-park hours. Creek flooding, underpass conditions, construction, drought work, maintenance, and Garrison corridor projects can affect segments.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Connected aquatic facilities, programs, shelter rentals, events, and nearby attractions may charge separately.
places.parking: Lineberger Park's Chestnut Street lot is the most developed central access. Additional access exists near Ferguson Park and Robinwood Road; use only signed public parking and plan a return for longer one-way trips.
places.restroom: Lineberger Park provides restrooms and water fountains during operating conditions. Do not assume continuous facilities along the creek corridor; verify amenities at the exact access point you choose.
places.accessibility: The principal route is paved, but grades, creek bridges, underpasses, crossings, flooding, construction detours, and trailhead connections vary. Current Garrison improvements may temporarily change the best step-free approach.
places.trail: The Catawba Creek section includes roughly 1.8 miles from Robinwood Road westward, while the connected Avon section reaches Lineberger Park and toward Ferguson Park. Consult the current City map for open extensions rather than relying on planned mileage.
places.family: A short out-and-back from Lineberger Park pairs the greenway with a playground, memorial, shelters, restrooms, and seasonal aquatic options. Supervise children around water, bridges, underpasses, crossings, and bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the greenway where posted rules permit. Keep leashes short around cyclists and crossings, remove waste, and follow rules at Lineberger and Ferguson parks.
places.picnic: Use designated lawns, tables, and shelters in connected parks rather than blocking the shared path. Reserve shelters for guaranteed group use.
places.landmarks: Key reference points include Lineberger Park and Vietnam War Memorial, Avon Creek, Catawba Creek, Ferguson Park, Robinwood Road, picnic lawn areas, the Garrison LEARNS underpass project, and Carolina Thread Trail connections.
places.closures: Creek flooding, storms, underpass work, Garrison LEARNS construction, greenway extensions, utility projects, and connected-park closures can interrupt sections. Check City notices after heavy rain and before a through-trip.

places.name: Pleasant Park
places.operator: Town of Apex Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
places.address: 3400 Pleasant Plains Road, Apex, NC 27502. After entering, turn left and then right onto Recreation Drive for the lots closest to Splashlantis and the Enchanted Forest playground.
places.summary: Pleasant Park is a 92-acre regional sports and family destination with the 1.5-acre inclusive Enchanted Forest playground, free seasonal Splashlantis splash pad, six multipurpose fields, tennis, pickleball and basketball courts, shelters, meeting rooms, and restrooms.
places.hours: The park is listed as open 5:30 am to 10 pm year-round; fields, courts, and restrooms open at 6:30 am. Basketball and pickleball courts operate from sunrise until about 30 minutes after sunset. Splashlantis has its own seasonal 10 am to 6 pm schedule when open.
places.cost: General park access, Enchanted Forest, courts during public availability, and Splashlantis are free. Fields, shelters, meeting rooms, programs, and organized events may require reservations or fees.
places.parking: Use the on-site lots and choose Recreation Drive for the closest approach to Splashlantis and Enchanted Forest. Parking is not allowed along Pleasant Plains Road; tournament and peak splash-pad periods can be busy.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at the fieldhouse and shelter areas and generally open at 6:30 am. Splashlantis operations and individual buildings may follow separate schedules.
places.accessibility: Enchanted Forest was designed with nine inclusive play villages for varied ages and abilities, and Splashlantis is open to all ages and abilities. Use signed accessible parking and paved approaches; individual play and water features vary.
places.trail: The park includes internal paved connections and a cross-country course. Do not assume every future trail or athletic feature shown in long-range plans has been built; follow the current park map and signs.
places.family: The strongest family pairing is Enchanted Forest plus Splashlantis during its season. Bring towels, sunscreen, and water shoes for the splash pad; adults must supervise children because there are no lifeguards.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled in permitted general park areas, remove waste, and keep pets out of playground and splash-pad surfaces, buildings, and active athletic areas unless posted otherwise.
places.picnic: The Forest Shelter is nearest the playground and the Fields Shelter is nearest the athletic fields. Reserve a shelter for guaranteed group use and confirm the correct shelter address before directing guests.
places.landmarks: Key orientation points are Recreation Drive, Enchanted Forest's nine play villages, Splashlantis, Forest Shelter, Fields Shelter, fieldhouse, multipurpose fields, and tennis, pickleball, and basketball courts.
places.closures: Splashlantis is seasonal: in 2026 it opens weekends beginning May 23, daily June 15 through Labor Day, then weekends through the last Sunday in September, 10 am to 6 pm. Weather, capacity, maintenance, tournaments, and field schedules can affect access.

places.name: Apex Community Park
places.operator: Town of Apex Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
places.address: Main park entrance: 2200 Laura Duncan Road, Apex, NC 27502. Lake Trail entrance: 1808 Lake Pine Drive, Cary, NC 27511. Use the Laura Duncan Road side for the designated vessel launch and main recreation facilities.
places.summary: Apex Community Park is a 160-acre destination surrounding a 50-plus-acre lake, with more than three miles of paved and natural trails, playgrounds, courts, athletic fields, fitness features, shelters, picnic areas, restrooms, an accessible fishing dock, and permitted small-vessel access.
places.hours: The Town lists the park as open daily from 6:30 am to 10 pm year-round. Fishing and boating are limited to 6:30 am through sunset, and fields, facilities, projects, and reservations may have separate availability.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, court, and picnic access is free. Fishing requires a Town of Apex permit and, for anglers age 16 and older, a North Carolina fishing license. Launching a vessel requires a Town seasonal permit; shelters and fields may have fees.
places.parking: Choose your entrance before arriving. Laura Duncan Road serves the main recreation area and the only designated hand-carry vessel launch; Lake Pine Drive serves the lake trail side. Lots can fill during leagues and events.
places.restroom: Restroom facilities serve the developed park areas. Their exact proximity depends on which entrance and activity area you use, so lake-trail visitors should plan around the current park map.
places.accessibility: The fishing pier is wheelchair accessible, and developed areas include paved routes. The Town is planning inclusive playground and ADA-route improvements; natural trail surfaces, grades, older routes, and construction conditions vary.
places.trail: The park has more than three miles of trails: about two miles of paved greenway and one mile of natural walking trail. The two entrances reach different portions of the lake loop, so confirm your intended route and turnaround.
places.family: Playgrounds, swings, lake views, trails, picnic areas, courts, and the fitness course support mixed-age visits. Swimming and wading are prohibited; supervise children closely near the lake, dock, launch, and bicycle traffic.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use permitted park and trail areas. Keep leashes short on shared paths, remove waste, and keep pets outside playgrounds, athletic fields, buildings, and other posted restricted areas.
places.picnic: Large and small shelters and picnic areas with grills are available. Reserve shelters for guaranteed group use and use the Laura Duncan Road entrance for the principal shelter and launch area.
places.landmarks: Important reference points include the Laura Duncan Road main entrance, Lake Pine Drive trail entrance, 50-plus-acre lake, wheelchair-accessible fishing dock, designated hand-carry vessel launch, playground, shelters, Elevate Fitness Course, hockey rinks, courts, and ball fields.
places.closures: The playground area is in a renovation planning process, and survey work or later construction may affect nearby routes. Athletic fields can close for turf renovation; check current Town maintenance notices before a field-dependent visit.

places.name: Apex Nature Park and Seymour Athletic Fields
places.operator: Town of Apex Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
places.address: Apex Nature Park entrance: 2600 Evans Road, Apex, NC 27502, for the amphitheater, disc golf, dog park, trails, large shelter, and restroom. Seymour Athletic Fields entrance: 2500 Evans Road for the playground, courts, fields, small shelter, trails, and restroom.
places.summary: This 160-plus-acre destination has two connected sections: Apex Nature Park for the amphitheater, disc golf, dog park, environmental stations, trails, shelter, and restroom; and Seymour Athletic Fields for a multi-age playground, lighted fields and courts, sand volleyball, shelter, trails, and restroom.
places.hours: The park is listed as open 5:30 am to 10 pm year-round; fields, courts, and restrooms open at 6:30 am. Programs, reservations, the dog park, amphitheater events, and athletic schedules may control access to individual facilities.
places.cost: General park, trail, playground, disc-golf, court, and amphitheater-lawn access is generally free when not reserved. Dog-park use requires registration, and shelters, fields, programs, and events may require reservations or fees.
places.parking: There are lots at both Evans Road entrances. Use 2600 Evans Road for the Nature Park amenities and 2500 Evans Road for Seymour Athletic Fields; a paved walkway connects the sections, but choosing the correct lot saves a long cross-park walk.
places.restroom: Each section has a restroom facility, generally opening at 6:30 am. Event, maintenance, and seasonal conditions may affect building availability.
places.accessibility: Paved paths connect major developed features and the two sections. Parking is available at both entrances; natural trails, disc-golf terrain, lawn seating, and individual play or athletic surfaces vary.
places.trail: The site has paved and natural multi-use trails, including the self-guided Apex Natural Heritage Trail with ten interpretive stops between Seymour Athletic Fields and the amphitheater. Follow signs to distinguish the connecting route from disc-golf fairways.
places.family: For playgrounds and court play, start at 2500 Evans Road. For the amphitheater, environmental stations, a walk, or disc golf, start at 2600 Evans Road. The connecting heritage trail can turn the two halves into one longer visit.
places.dogs: The registered dog park is on the 2600 Evans Road Nature Park side. Elsewhere keep dogs leashed, remove waste, and avoid playgrounds, fields, courts, buildings, and disc-golf play lines as posted.
places.picnic: A large shelter is on the Nature Park side and a small shelter is near Seymour Athletic Fields. Reserve for guaranteed group use and direct guests to the matching entrance.
places.landmarks: Nature Park landmarks include the amphitheater, disc-golf course, dog park, environmental stations, solar-served restroom, large shelter, and heritage trail. Seymour landmarks include the playground, multipurpose fields, tennis and pickleball courts, sand volleyball, small shelter, and restroom.
places.closures: Athletic fields may close for turf renovation, weather, or reservations. Dog-park registration, amphitheater events, maintenance, and field schedules can limit specific amenities even while the broader park remains open.

places.name: Kelly Road Park
places.operator: Town of Apex Parks, Recreation and Cultural Resources
places.address: 1609 Kelly Road, Apex, NC 27502. This is also a developed access point for the Beaver Creek Greenway, with parking, restrooms, playgrounds, courts, field, and shelter nearby.
places.summary: Kelly Road Park is a 25-acre neighborhood and greenway destination with separate playgrounds for ages 2-5 and 5-12, a picnic shelter and grill, lighted softball field, full-size and junior tennis/pickleball courts, basketball court, restrooms, and a Beaver Creek Greenway trailhead.
places.hours: The Town lists the park as open daily from 6:30 am to 10 pm year-round. The connecting Beaver Creek Greenway is open dawn to dusk, and fields, courts, restrooms, renovation work, and reservations may have separate availability.
places.cost: General park, playground, court, trail, and picnic access is free. Shelter, field, programs, leagues, and organized uses may require reservations or fees.
places.parking: Use the on-site Kelly Road lot for the playgrounds, shelter, courts, softball field, restrooms, and Beaver Creek Greenway. Peak league and playground periods can fill the closest spaces; use only signed public parking.
places.restroom: Restroom facilities are available near the developed recreation area. Renovation assessments and future KidsTowne work may temporarily change access, so check current Town notices.
places.accessibility: Developed paths connect much of the park and the greenway trailhead. The KidsTowne renovation is intended to update the playground area; construction, older play features, court access, and greenway transitions may vary.
places.trail: Kelly Road Park is a trailhead for the paved Beaver Creek Greenway, currently extending toward Jaycee Park through boardwalk, asphalt, concrete, and neighborhood connections. Greenway hours are dawn to dusk; plan an out-and-back unless you arrange a pickup.
places.family: Two age-banded playgrounds, the loop connections, shelter, courts, field, and greenway make this a flexible family stop. Check renovation status before promising a particular KidsTowne feature.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use permitted park and greenway areas. Keep leashes short around cyclists and play areas, remove waste, and stay outside playgrounds, fields, courts, buildings, and other posted restricted spaces.
places.picnic: A reservable picnic shelter with a grill serves the park. Reserve for guaranteed group use and keep the greenway clear when gathering nearby.
places.landmarks: Key reference points are the KidsTowne playground area, younger- and older-child play zones, picnic shelter, softball field, full-size and junior tennis/pickleball courts, basketball court, restroom, and Beaver Creek Greenway trailhead.
places.closures: The KidsTowne playground renovation is in design, with completion still to be determined. The playground remains subject to future construction impacts; weather, field work, restroom work, and greenway maintenance can also affect individual facilities.

places.name: Jacksonville Commons Recreation Complex
places.operator: City of Jacksonville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 100 Recreation Lane, Jacksonville, NC 28546. The campus also includes Richard Ray All America Park at 1200 Commons Drive North and a free Park & Ride lot at 100 Recreation Loop.
places.summary: Known locally as The Commons, this is Jacksonville's largest city recreation campus, combining baseball and softball fields, soccer, tennis, multiple play areas, an amphitheater, Gardens of the States, meditation labyrinth, Richard Ray All America Park, trails, indoor gymnasium, adult center, restrooms, and event space.
places.hours: Outdoor Commons park areas are listed as open 7 am to 9 pm, while the Recreation Complex listing gives 7 am to 11 pm. Buildings, fields, courts, programs, and events follow separate schedules; use the posted hours for the exact facility you plan to visit.
places.cost: General outdoor park and garden access is free. Open-recreation programs may be free with registration, while gym, meeting rooms, fields, leagues, classes, rentals, and special events may require fees.
places.parking: Use 100 Recreation Lane for the central recreation buildings. The free 187-space Park & Ride at 100 Recreation Loop can also serve as a park-and-walk access point; large tournaments and Jamboree events can change traffic and available parking.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available in the Commons Recreation Center and around developed athletic and play areas when those facilities are open. Building hours may differ from outdoor park hours.
places.accessibility: The campus has multiple paved approaches, sidewalk and trail connections, transit access, accessible parking, and indoor recreation. Distances between fields, gardens, play areas, and buildings are substantial, so choose the closest arrival point.
places.trail: Internal walking routes connect the recreation buildings, fields, gardens, amphitheater, playgrounds, and surrounding campus. This is a multi-node complex rather than a single compact loop; use the current site map for a specific destination.
places.family: Multiple play areas, Richard Ray All America Park, gardens, sports fields, indoor recreation, and major family events make this a full-day-capable destination. Check field and program calendars before promising open play.
places.dogs: Pets must be leashed at no more than six feet in permitted outdoor areas. Remove waste and keep animals outside playgrounds, fields, courts, buildings, gardens, and event zones where posted.
places.picnic: Picnic and gathering spaces are distributed through the campus. Reserve shelters or indoor rooms for guaranteed group use; inflatables are prohibited in city parks.
places.landmarks: Key wayfinding points are the Recreation Admin building, gymnasium, Adult Center, amphitheater, Gardens of the States, meditation labyrinth, Richard Ray All America Park, baseball and softball complexes, soccer fields, tennis courts, and Park & Ride.
places.closures: Leagues, tournaments, Jacksonville's Jamboree, maintenance, rentals, and City programs can reserve fields, courts, buildings, parking, or event lawns. Verify the exact facility calendar before an activity-dependent visit.

places.name: Riverwalk Crossing Park
places.operator: City of Jacksonville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 421 Court Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540. The downtown waterfront route continues toward L.P. Willingham Park, Kerr Street Park, and Riverwalk Marina at 15 Kerr Street.
places.summary: Riverwalk Crossing Park is Jacksonville's landscaped downtown New River event park, with a public stage, waterfront paths, garden areas, vendor-ready streets, river views, and connections toward nearby waterfront parks, a gazebo, and Riverwalk Marina.
places.hours: The City lists Riverwalk Crossing Park as open daily from 7 am to 9 pm. Scheduled festivals, stage events, setup, weather, waterfront conditions, and neighboring marina operations can affect access.
places.cost: General park and waterfront-walk access is free. Festivals may have vendors or paid activities, and stage, marina, shelter, or organized uses may require reservations and fees.
places.parking: Use legal downtown public parking near Court Street and walk into the park. Event days can close streets or repurpose nearby spaces; vehicles are not allowed on the grass or paved park areas.
places.restroom: Do not assume a restroom is immediately beside every section of the Riverwalk. Facilities may be available at nearby downtown recreation or marina nodes during their operating hours; plan ahead for large events.
places.accessibility: The core park uses paved downtown and waterfront approaches. Event barriers, lawn areas, curb transitions, marina grades, and temporary vendor layouts can change the easiest step-free route.
places.trail: Landscaped walkways lead toward the New River and connect with the broader downtown waterfront network. Treat this as an urban waterfront walk rather than a long natural trail.
places.family: The river view, open lawn, gardens, gazebo connection, and seasonal festivals work well for a short family visit. There is no conventional playground listed at this park; supervise children closely at the water's edge.
places.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed where posted, with a maximum six-foot leash. Remove waste and avoid event crowds, stage areas, landscaped beds, and waterfront edges when conditions are unsafe.
places.picnic: Use designated seating and nearby waterfront gathering areas without blocking paths or event setup. Organized use of the stage or park requires City coordination.
places.landmarks: Orientation points include the Court Street entrance, public stage, long garden area, New River waterfront, downstream gazebo, nearby L.P. Willingham Park, Kerr Street Park, and Riverwalk Marina.
places.closures: Oktoberfest, Winterfest, National Night Out, other festivals, stage reservations, storm conditions, flood or waterfront work, and event setup may limit normal access or parking.

places.name: Wilson Bay Park
places.operator: City of Jacksonville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 5 West Bayshore Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540. Parking is limited to the signed on-site lot; the City states that on-street parking is not permitted for shelter use.
places.summary: Wilson Bay Park is one of Jacksonville's busiest passive waterfront parks, offering Wilson Bay views, fishing access, a boardwalk, gazebo, playground, reservable shelter, picnic tables, grills, restrooms, benches, shade, and shoreline habitat near the New River.
places.hours: The park is open daily from 7 am to 9 pm. Shelter reservations are limited to four hours, and future seawall, boardwalk, or gazebo work may affect individual waterfront features.
places.cost: General park, playground, waterfront, and fishing access is free. The shelter is listed at $15 per hour with a maximum reservation occupancy of 30; fishing license requirements still apply.
places.parking: Use the small on-site parking lot. Parking is limited, and the shelter rules prohibit on-street overflow parking, so arrive early or choose another waterfront park during peak periods.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available near the shelter and playground. Hours and availability can be affected by maintenance or construction.
places.accessibility: The City ADA assessment documented an accessible parking space, compliant approach, curb ramp, and shelter entrance. Boardwalk conditions, sand playground surfacing, shoreline work, and individual fishing positions may vary.
places.trail: This is a compact waterfront park with a boardwalk rather than a long trail system. Use the shoreline route for bay views and fishing, but do not expect a continuous loop around Wilson Bay.
places.family: The playground, shaded shelter, picnic tables, restrooms, bay views, and fishing make this a useful short family stop. Supervise children around the shoreline and boardwalk.
places.dogs: Pets must remain on a leash no longer than six feet. Remove waste and keep dogs away from playground equipment, shelter food areas, fishing lines, and posted construction zones.
places.picnic: The waterfront shelter includes picnic tables and serves groups up to 30 by reservation. Grills are available; extinguish coals fully, and note that amplified music is not allowed.
places.landmarks: Look for the waterfront shelter, playground, restrooms, Wilson Bay boardwalk, gazebo, fishing edge, benches, shade trees, and the Route 17/Buddy Phillips Bridge view.
places.closures: A City capital project plans replacement of the aging seawall, boardwalk, and gazebo, with design and later construction capable of affecting waterfront access. Check City notices before a boardwalk- or fishing-dependent visit.

places.name: Sturgeon City Park
places.operator: City of Jacksonville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 110 Loyola Drive, Jacksonville, NC 28540. The park sits on Wilson Bay near the Sturgeon City environmental education campus; confirm whether your program meets in the public park or a campus building.
places.summary: Sturgeon City Park is a quiet public Wilson Bay waterfront stop associated with Jacksonville's environmental-education district, offering shoreline views, walking and cycling access, fishing, open green space, and proximity to Sturgeon City programs and restored natural areas.
places.hours: The City lists the public park as open daily from 7 am to 9 pm. Sturgeon City educational buildings, programs, events, and rentals operate on separate schedules and should not be assumed open with the park.
places.cost: General public park, waterfront, and fishing access is free. Educational programs, events, camps, rentals, and fishing licenses may involve separate registration or fees.
places.parking: Use the public access at 110 Loyola Drive and follow signs for park versus program parking. Event and education-campus use can change the closest available spaces.
places.restroom: Do not rely on Sturgeon City campus buildings being open during all public park hours. Confirm restroom availability with the City or program operator before a long visit.
places.accessibility: Developed waterfront and campus approaches include paved areas, but shoreline grades, natural surfaces, fishing edges, and building access vary. Confirm accommodations for a scheduled program directly.
places.trail: Use the park for a short Wilson Bay walk and connections through the environmental-education area. It is not documented as a long standalone trail; nearby downtown waterfront parks provide additional walking options.
places.family: This is best for a quiet bay view, fishing, nature observation, or pairing with a scheduled Sturgeon City educational program. It is not listed as a conventional playground destination.
places.dogs: Leashed pets may use permitted public outdoor areas under City park rules. Keep them away from education activities, wildlife areas, fishing lines, buildings, and posted restricted zones.
places.picnic: Open green space may support a simple picnic where posted, but do not assume campus rooms or event spaces are freely available. Keep paths and program areas clear.
places.landmarks: Key references are the Loyola Drive entrance, Wilson Bay shoreline, Sturgeon City environmental education buildings, natural restoration areas, fishing access, and views toward the New River corridor.
places.closures: Programs, private events, shoreline work, storms, flooding, and campus operations may affect parking or specific areas. Verify building access separately from the public park.

places.name: Northeast Creek Park
places.operator: City of Jacksonville Recreation and Parks
places.address: 910 Corbin Road, Jacksonville, NC 28546. The City splash-pad page also uses 911 Corbin Street; follow park signs for the playground/splash-pad side versus the boat and trailer parking area.
places.summary: Northeast Creek Park combines an inclusive playground and free seasonal splash pad with two lighted softball fields, picnic shelters, restrooms, a regulation 18-hole wooded disc-golf course, fishing, green space, and a two-lane boat and kayak launch with trailer parking.
places.hours: General City park hours are 7 am to 9 pm. Playground-side shelter restrooms are closed from 9 pm to 7 am. In 2026 the splash pad operates daily 10 am to 7 pm from May 23 through September 27, subject to closures.
places.cost: General park, playground, splash pad, disc golf, fishing-area, and launch access is free. Fishing licenses, field or shelter reservations, programs, and organized uses may have requirements or fees.
places.parking: Choose the correct on-site area: boat and trailer spaces serve the two-lane launch, while family parking serves the inclusive playground, splash pad, shelters, and fields. Do not occupy trailer spaces for ordinary park use.
places.restroom: Bathroom facilities serve the developed park. The restrooms at the shelter on the playground side are specifically closed from 9 pm to 7 am; project work can temporarily change access.
places.accessibility: The inclusive playground serves varied ages and abilities, and the zero-entry, zero-depth splash pad offers water wheelchairs by advance arrangement. A future restoration adds an ADA-compliant kayak launch; do not represent that planned feature as complete yet.
places.trail: The regulation disc-golf course mixes open and tight wooded holes with white beginner/amateur tees and longer blue advanced tees. Stay alert for flying discs and do not treat fairways as ordinary walking paths.
places.family: The inclusive playground, splash pad, shade, picnic benches, shelters, restrooms, and fishing make this a strong family destination. Children under ten require adult supervision at the splash pad, and no animals are allowed on its surface.
places.dogs: Pets must be leashed at no more than six feet in allowed park areas and are prohibited on the splash pad. Keep dogs clear of playgrounds, fields, shelters with food, boat ramps, and disc-golf flight paths.
places.picnic: Shelters and shaded picnic benches sit near the family amenities. Reservations do not guarantee splash-pad operation, and the City does not refund shelter fees when the splash pad has a problem or closure.
places.landmarks: Orientation points include the inclusive playground, seasonal splash pad, two softball fields, picnic shelters, playground-side restroom, white and blue disc-golf tees, fishing area, two-lane boat ramp, kayak access, and trailer lot.
places.closures: The existing waterfront boardwalk was scheduled for removal beginning May 2026 for safety, ahead of a restoration extending into 2027 with a new boardwalk, fishing pier, living shoreline, wetlands work, and accessible kayak launch. Expect construction impacts near the launch and waterfront.

places.name: Latta Nature Preserve
places.operator: Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation
places.address: Use Quest Nature Center at 6345 Sample Road, Huntersville, NC 28078 for staffed visitor information and trail orientation. Other preserve trail, equestrian, water, and partner-facility access points may use different gates.
places.summary: Latta Nature Preserve protects a large Lake Norman peninsula with an extensive network of hiking and horseback-riding trails, shoreline and paddling access, wildlife habitat, picnic areas, Quest Nature Center, and the separately operated Carolina Raptor Center.
places.hours: The nature preserve is open daily from sunup to sundown. Quest Nature Center is open Monday-Saturday 9 am-5 pm and Sunday 1-5 pm. Partner facilities, programs, gates, water access, and equestrian areas may have separate hours.
places.cost: General preserve and trail access is free. Quest's exhibit hall is generally part of the public nature-center experience, while registered programs, rentals, and the separately operated Carolina Raptor Center may charge admission or fees.
places.parking: Choose the access point for your activity before arriving. Quest at 6345 Sample Road is the best staffed orientation point; trail, horse, paddling, and Raptor Center destinations are spread across the preserve and are not all adjacent.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at Quest Nature Center during building hours and may be available at other developed nodes. Do not assume facilities on remote trails; plan around your selected trailhead.
places.accessibility: Quest includes an interactive exhibit hall, aquarium, classrooms, and developed access. Preserve trails range in surface and grade, and shoreline, equestrian, and natural routes may not be step-free; request specific accommodation information before visiting.
places.trail: The preserve is known for an extensive hiking and equestrian network through forest and along Mountain Island Lake. Carry the current trail map, stay on the correct use-designated route, and allow time to return before sundown.
places.family: Quest's live native animals, aquarium, exhibits, and nearby trails make a strong family starting point. Longer trails, shoreline access, and the Raptor Center can extend the visit, but each has different needs and schedules.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and under control where permitted, yield to horses, remove waste, and observe restrictions in nature-center buildings, wildlife exhibits, sensitive habitat, and partner facilities.
places.picnic: Use designated picnic areas and reservable shelters without disturbing habitat or blocking trailheads. Confirm the exact shelter location because the preserve covers a large area.
places.landmarks: Major orientation points include Quest Nature Center, its 6,000-gallon aquarium and live-animal exhibits, Sample Road, Mountain Island Lake shoreline, hiking and equestrian trailheads, paddling access, picnic areas, and the separate Carolina Raptor Center.
places.closures: Storms, high water, prescribed burns, natural-resource work, trail conditions, heat, and special programs can affect access. Preserve hours end at sundown even when a partner facility lists a different schedule.

places.name: North Mecklenburg Park
places.operator: Town of Huntersville Parks and Recreation
places.address: 16131 Old Statesville Road, Huntersville, NC 28078. The park entrance is along NC 115/Old Statesville Road; follow internal signs to the correct fields, courts, playground, or disc-golf area.
places.summary: North Mecklenburg Park is a large county-owned, Town-operated community sports park with baseball and softball fields, soccer or multipurpose space, tennis, basketball, playgrounds, picnic facilities, trails, and a wooded disc-golf course.
places.hours: Use posted Town park and facility hours; lighted courts and scheduled fields can operate differently from passive areas. Confirm current closing time and field status before an evening or league-dependent visit.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, and casual recreation access is free. Reserved fields, courts, leagues, tournaments, shelters, and organized uses may require Town approval or fees.
places.parking: Multiple activity areas are spread through the park. Follow internal signs and park near your specific field, court, playground, or disc-golf starting area rather than assuming one central lot serves everything equally.
places.restroom: Restrooms serve developed recreation areas, but proximity and opening schedules vary by field complex and activity node. Confirm availability for early, late, or tournament visits.
places.accessibility: Developed parking and paved approaches serve major sports and play areas. Field edges, older playground routes, wooded trails, and disc-golf terrain vary in grade and surface.
places.trail: The park includes walking connections and a disc-golf course through wooded terrain. Stay clear of active fairways, watch for flying discs, and use a current course or park map.
places.family: Playgrounds, ball fields, courts, open space, picnic areas, and short walks support mixed-age visits. Tournament activity can make the park busy, so check schedules when seeking casual play.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed where permitted, remove waste, and stay outside playgrounds, active fields, courts, buildings, and disc-golf throwing lanes unless signs say otherwise.
places.picnic: Use designated tables and shelters and reserve group facilities for guaranteed use. Keep grills and gatherings away from fields, trails, and play surfaces.
places.landmarks: Key wayfinding points are the Old Statesville Road entrance, baseball and softball complexes, multipurpose fields, tennis and basketball courts, playgrounds, picnic facilities, wooded trail areas, and disc-golf course.
places.closures: Field maintenance, rain, tournaments, reservations, construction, and seasonal schedules can close individual sports areas while the broader park remains open.

places.name: Holbrook Park
places.operator: Town of Huntersville Parks and Recreation
places.address: 100 Sherwood Drive, Huntersville, NC 28078, beside Huntersville Elementary School. From Gilead Road, turn onto Sherwood Drive; the park entrance and lot are on the right.
places.summary: Holbrook Park is a compact shaded neighborhood recreation park with a multi-age playground, swings, tennis and dedicated pickleball courts, a covered picnic pavilion, grills, restrooms, benches, nature-trail connections, and access toward downtown Huntersville.
places.hours: Commonly published park hours are 8 am to 10 pm daily, but verify posted gate and court hours before late-evening play. Court reservations and Town programs may affect availability.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, and open courts are free. Some pickleball or tennis courts may be reservable, with nonresident reservation fees or program charges; open-play courts remain subject to posted rules.
places.parking: Use the on-site Sherwood Drive lot. The park is compact, but school activity, court demand, and group pavilion use can fill the closest spaces.
places.restroom: A public restroom facility serves the playground, courts, and pavilion area. Posted opening and maintenance conditions control availability.
places.accessibility: The park has on-site parking and developed routes to major amenities. Court gates, playground surfacing, nature-trail sections, and older grades may vary; use signed accessible spaces and paved approaches.
places.trail: A short nature-trail and greenway connection supports walks toward the surrounding neighborhood and downtown. Confirm the current connection if planning a through-route rather than a park loop.
places.family: The shaded playground, swings, pavilion, restrooms, courts, and short trail make this an easy family stop. The play area includes elements for younger and older children.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled, remove waste, and keep pets outside playgrounds, courts, restrooms, and food-service areas of the pavilion.
places.picnic: The covered pavilion and grills support picnics and parties. Reserve through the Town for guaranteed group use and leave court and trail access clear.
places.landmarks: Look for the Sherwood Drive lot, Huntersville Elementary School, shaded forest-themed playground, swing set, pavilion, restrooms, tennis courts, dedicated pickleball courts, benches, and nature-trail entrance.
places.closures: Court resurfacing, reservations, school activity, maintenance, storms, and Town programs may affect specific amenities. Confirm court availability before a pickleball- or tennis-dependent trip.

places.name: Torrence Creek Greenway
places.operator: Mecklenburg County Park and Recreation
places.address: A developed access is available near the Huntersville Gateway Park & Ride at Compass Street. The connected McDowell Creek, Torrence Creek, and Torrence Tributary system extends between neighborhood access points near Chilgrove Lane, Cedar River Road, Compass Street, and Rosewood Meadow Lane.
places.summary: Torrence Creek Greenway is part of a 3.72-mile connected Mecklenburg County greenway system through Huntersville, linking creek corridors, neighborhoods, urban trails, and the Gateway Park & Ride, with a newer tributary segment reaching Rosewood Meadow Lane.
places.hours: Use the greenway during daylight and posted access-point hours. County greenways can close for flooding, storms, bridge or pavement work, utility projects, and habitat maintenance.
places.cost: General greenway access is free. Transit fares, nearby private parking, programs, and unrelated facilities may charge separately.
places.parking: The Gateway Park & Ride near Compass Street is a practical access point. Other entrances are neighborhood connections with limited or no dedicated parking; use only signed public spaces and do not block residential streets.
places.restroom: Do not assume restrooms or water are available along the linear corridor. Plan around developed nearby parks or businesses and carry water.
places.accessibility: The principal greenway is paved, but access ramps, road crossings, grades, bridge transitions, flood debris, and neighborhood connectors vary. Check current conditions after storms.
places.trail: The County lists 3.72 miles for the connected McDowell Creek, Torrence Creek, and Torrence Tributary greenways from near Chilgrove Lane to Cedar River Road and Compass Street. A newer 0.9-mile tributary segment reaches Rosewood Meadow Lane.
places.family: Choose a short out-and-back from Compass Street for a simple family walk or ride. Supervise children at crossings, bridges, neighborhood exits, and around faster cyclists.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome where posted. Keep leashes short on shared paths, remove waste, and yield to cyclists, runners, and other users.
places.picnic: This is primarily a travel and exercise corridor. Use designated seating or nearby parks rather than gathering across the trail or on sensitive creek banks.
places.landmarks: Useful reference points include Torrence Creek, McDowell Creek, the Torrence Tributary, Huntersville Gateway Park & Ride, Compass Street, Rosewood Meadow Lane, Cedar River Road, Chilgrove Lane, neighborhood exits, bridges, and mile markers.
places.closures: Creek flooding, fallen trees, bridge inspections, pavement work, utility projects, and construction can interrupt segments. After heavy rain, verify conditions and be prepared to turn around.

places.name: Southern Community Park
places.operator: Town of Chapel Hill Parks and Recreation
places.address: North entrance: 100 Sumac Road, Chapel Hill, NC 27516. South entrance: 1000 Dogwood Acres Drive. Choose the entrance nearest your field, playground, dog park, shelter, court, or Fan Branch Trail destination.
places.summary: Southern Community Park is a large recreation destination with natural-grass multipurpose fields, playground, dog park, basketball and pickleball courts, inline hockey, disc golf, picnic shelters, restrooms, open lawns, and the paved Fan Branch Trail fitness circuit.
places.hours: The park is open dawn to dusk. Its fields are not lighted, and individual courts, rentals, dog-park conditions, and scheduled activities may have separate availability.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, dog park, open courts, and picnic access are free. Fields, courts, shelters, programs, and organized uses may require reservations and fees.
places.parking: Paved parking is available at the park's entrances. Parking is prohibited along Dogwood Acres Drive, so choose the correct lot and do not rely on roadside overflow during tournaments.
places.restroom: Public restrooms serve the developed park and shelter area. Their proximity varies by entrance and activity node; availability can be affected by maintenance or seasonal operations.
places.accessibility: Paved lots and the 10-foot-wide Fan Branch Trail provide developed access, and major recreation areas have paved approaches. Some grass fields, disc-golf terrain, slopes, and individual play features vary.
places.trail: Fan Branch Trail is a roughly 1.62-mile paved woodland route with an ExoFit fitness course and a few steep slopes. Disc-golf fairways are separate recreation space; stay alert when crossing them.
places.family: The playground, lawns, shelters, courts, trail, and fitness stations support mixed-age visits. The dog park and sports fields can be busy, so use the entrance closest to your primary activity.
places.dogs: Use the designated dog park for off-leash activity and leash dogs elsewhere. Remove waste and keep pets outside playgrounds, fields, courts, shelters with food, and restricted areas.
places.picnic: Picnic areas and reservable shelters are available, including a larger shelter. Reserve for guaranteed group use and direct guests to the matching entrance.
places.landmarks: Key wayfinding points are the Sumac Road north entrance, Dogwood Acres south entrance, playground, dog park, large and small shelters, multipurpose fields, basketball and pickleball courts, inline hockey rink, disc-golf course, Fan Branch Trail, and fitness circuit.
places.closures: Natural-grass fields close seasonally in summer and winter and may close after rain. Reservations, maintenance, trail work, and tournaments can affect individual areas while the park remains open.

places.name: Cedar Falls Park
places.operator: Town of Chapel Hill Parks and Recreation
places.address: 501 Weaver Dairy Road, Chapel Hill, NC 27514, across from East Chapel Hill High School. Use the main park lot for fields, playground, shelter, restrooms, tennis area, and Cedar Falls Trail.
places.summary: Cedar Falls Park combines three lighted turf multipurpose fields, two lighted youth baseball fields, one lighted adult baseball field, a playground, shelter, restrooms, six tennis courts, and a 1.5-mile natural-surface creek-side trail.
places.hours: The park and natural trail are open dawn to dusk. Lighted athletic facilities may operate until 11 pm when scheduled. Tennis courts remain listed as closed for reconstruction until the Town announces reopening.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, and casual access are free. Fields, tennis courts when reopened, shelter, programs, and organized uses may require reservations and fees.
places.parking: Use the large main lot at 501 Weaver Dairy Road. Parking-lot paving and striping work has been phased to keep most spaces open, but construction and tournament demand can reduce capacity.
places.restroom: Restrooms serve the developed field, playground, and shelter area. Hours may track park operations, field schedules, and construction access.
places.accessibility: The Town describes the main parking area as ADA compliant and is completing an ADA-compliant sidewalk as part of the tennis reconstruction. The natural trail has variable soil, roots, grades, and wet conditions.
places.trail: Cedar Falls Trail is a 1.5-mile natural-surface route through creek-side and passive-recreation areas with neighborhood connections. Expect mud after rain and return before dusk.
places.family: The playground, shelter, ball fields, benches, restrooms, and creek-side trail make a flexible family visit. Do not promise tennis until the Town posts that reconstruction is complete and courts are open.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled, remove waste, and stay outside playgrounds, fields, courts, buildings, and posted construction zones.
places.picnic: A reservable shelter and picnic area serve the park. Reserve for guaranteed group use and check construction or tournament schedules before directing a large group.
places.landmarks: Look for the Weaver Dairy Road entrance, East Chapel Hill High School opposite the park, main lot, three turf fields, youth and adult baseball fields, playground, shelter, restrooms, six-court tennis complex, and Cedar Falls Trail entrance.
places.closures: The six lighted tennis courts are currently listed as closed for reconstruction. Parking improvements and final electrical, sidewalk, plaza, bleacher, and landscaping work may affect nearby access; athletic reservations and weather affect fields.

places.name: Homestead Park
places.operator: Town of Chapel Hill Parks and Recreation
places.address: 100 Aquatic Drive, Chapel Hill, NC 27516 for the outdoor park. Homestead Aquatic Center is a separate building at 300 Aquatic Drive with its own hours, admission, and pool schedule.
places.summary: Homestead Park is a large multi-use campus with lighted artificial-turf youth fields, baseball and softball fields, batting cages, basketball, playground, picnic shelter, restrooms, a 0.2-acre dog park, skate park, wooded hiking trails, and the adjacent indoor Homestead Aquatic Center.
places.hours: Outdoor park hours are dawn to 10 pm, with lighted facilities potentially operating until 11 pm when scheduled. The Aquatic Center has separate weekly hours and holiday closures; check its current pool schedule before visiting.
places.cost: General outdoor park, playground, trails, dog park, basketball, and skate-park access are free when not reserved. Fields, shelter, programs, skate-park rentals, and Aquatic Center swimming may require fees or registration.
places.parking: Use 100 Aquatic Drive for the outdoor park and 300 Aquatic Drive for the pool building. Lots serve different activity nodes and can fill during leagues, swim programs, and tournaments.
places.restroom: Outdoor restrooms serve the park, while the Aquatic Center has indoor changing and restroom facilities only during building hours. Do not rely on pool-building access for an early or late outdoor visit.
places.accessibility: Paved parking and routes serve major developed amenities, and the Aquatic Center is a staffed indoor facility. Wooded trails, field edges, dog-park surfacing, skate features, and individual play equipment vary.
places.trail: Natural wooded hiking paths provide a quieter alternative to the athletic campus. Surfaces and grades vary, especially after rain; follow park signs rather than crossing reserved fields.
places.family: The playground, fields, basketball, skate park, trails, shelter, dog park, and optional indoor pools support varied family interests. Pool access is a separate visit decision with its own schedule and fees.
places.dogs: Use the 0.2-acre dog park for designated off-leash activity and leash dogs elsewhere. Remove waste and keep pets outside playgrounds, fields, courts, skate surfaces, shelters with food, and the Aquatic Center.
places.picnic: A reservable picnic shelter and picnic area serve the outdoor park. Reserve for guaranteed use and identify the outdoor park address rather than the pool entrance for guests.
places.landmarks: Major nodes are the 100 Aquatic Drive outdoor entrance, 300 Aquatic Drive Aquatic Center, turf fields, baseball and softball fields, batting cages, basketball court, playground, shelter, dog park, skate park, restrooms, and wooded trails.
places.closures: Field schedules, seasonal grass-field closures, weather, tournaments, skate events, maintenance, and Aquatic Center holiday or program schedules can affect individual amenities.

places.name: Bolin Creek Trail
places.operator: Town of Chapel Hill Parks and Recreation
places.address: Primary accessible arrival: Chapel Hill Community Center Park, 120 South Estes Drive, Chapel Hill, NC 27514. Additional parking is available at Umstead Park, 399 Umstead Drive, and along Bolinwood Drive where legal.
places.summary: Bolin Creek Trail is a 10-foot-wide paved greenway through meadow and wooded floodplain, running roughly 1.5 to 2 miles between Community Center Park and Umstead Park and extending to about 2.5 miles with Tanyard Branch Trail toward Northside and downtown.
places.hours: The greenway is open dawn to dusk. Connected Community Center Park and Umstead Park have later posted park hours, but trail travel should still be completed before dusk.
places.cost: General trail use and park access are free. Indoor recreation, pools, rentals, programs, and nearby paid parking may charge separately.
places.parking: Community Center Park, Umstead Park, and legal spaces along Bolinwood Drive provide access. Community Center is the strongest accessible arrival point; choose Umstead for the Tanyard Branch and Northside end.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at Community Center Park and Umstead Park during their facility or park operations. There are no continuous facilities along the creek corridor.
places.accessibility: The principal trail is paved, about ten feet wide, and includes ADA access points. Flood debris, wet pavement, bridge approaches, construction, and connected natural trails can change conditions.
places.trail: The core paved route connects Community Center Park to Umstead Park; Tanyard Branch extends toward Northside and downtown, while Battle Branch connects toward UNC with natural surfaces and separate bicycle restrictions.
places.family: A short out-and-back from Community Center Park pairs the trail with an inclusive playground, rose garden, picnic area, and restrooms. Umstead adds a playground, shelters, basketball, volleyball, and restrooms.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the trail. Keep leashes short around cyclists and runners, remove waste, and follow connected-park restrictions.
places.picnic: Use picnic areas at Community Center Park or Umstead Park rather than blocking the greenway or disturbing creek banks. Shelters may require reservations.
places.landmarks: Useful references are Community Center Park, South Estes Drive, Bolin Creek, Bolinwood Drive, Umstead Park, Tanyard Branch Trail, Northside, Battle Branch Trail, bridges, meadow sections, wooded floodplain, and mile markers.
places.closures: Flooding, storms, fallen trees, bridge or pavement work, and nearby transit or road construction can affect access. Check Town notices after heavy rain and be ready to turn around at high water.

places.name: Burlington City Park
places.operator: City of Burlington Recreation and Parks
places.address: Main park address: 1388 Main Street, Burlington, NC 27215. The Splash Park uses 1400 Overbrook Road, and individual athletic, aquatic, pickleball, tennis, event, and amusement destinations have different internal approaches.
places.summary: Burlington's flagship park centers on the historic Dentzel Menagerie Carousel and also includes a miniature train and kiddie rides, ADA-inclusive playground, splash park, aquatic center, pickleball and tennis complexes, five softball fields, walking tracks, fitness equipment, shelters, amphitheater, dog park, and event spaces.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open daily sunrise to sunset. Amusement rides follow a seasonal weekly schedule, generally weekends year-round with additional Friday and summer weekday hours; all ride operations are weather permitting. Aquatic and splash facilities have separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, walking, and open-space access are free. Ride tickets cost $1 each; the carousel and train require two tickets, other kiddie rides one. The Splash Park is free with registration and capacity limits. Aquatics, courts, rentals, and programs may charge separately.
places.parking: Choose the entrance for your destination rather than relying on one central space. Main Street serves the park core; Overbrook Road is useful for the Splash Park and nearby facilities. Festivals and tournaments can change traffic and fill lots.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available around developed park, amusement, splash, aquatic, shelter, and athletic nodes during their operating periods. Individual buildings and concessions do not remain open for all park hours.
places.accessibility: The park includes an ADA-inclusive playground and an accessible miniature-train car. The train ramp cannot accommodate powered wheelchairs and has a 600-pound maximum; contact staff for current boarding details. Paved routes serve major facilities.
places.trail: Walking tracks, greenway links, and internal paths connect many park nodes. The campus is large, so use a current map and do not assume every attraction is a short walk from the same parking area.
places.family: The carousel, train, kiddie rides, inclusive playground, free seasonal Splash Park, picnic areas, and events make this a major family destination. Check ride height limits, weather, splash registration, and attraction hours before promising a full itinerary.
places.dogs: Use the designated Jiggs Askew Dog Park for off-leash activity and leash dogs elsewhere. Pets are not appropriate in ride queues, playgrounds, splash or aquatic areas, courts, fields, buildings, and food-service spaces.
places.picnic: Open-air and enclosed shelters, gazebos, grills, tables, lawns, and event spaces support gatherings. Reserve for guaranteed group use and specify the exact facility when directing guests.
places.landmarks: Key landmarks include the Carousel House and 1906-1910 Dentzel carousel, miniature train and tunnel, planes, cars and boats rides, concessions, inclusive playground, Splash Park, Maynard Aquatic Center, pickleball and tennis complexes, softball fields, Jimmy Combs Stage, shelters, and walking track.
places.closures: Rides are weather permitting and close on New Year's Day, Easter, Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. Splash, aquatic, field, court, festival, and construction schedules can affect individual areas while the general park remains open.

places.name: Arboretum at Willowbrook Park
places.operator: City of Burlington Recreation and Parks
places.address: 315 West Willowbrook Drive, Burlington, NC 27215. The 17-acre linear park stretches toward East Willowbrook Drive between Church Street and Front Street; follow signs for the Commons Building, accessible Treehouse, and Veterans Overlook.
places.summary: The Burlington Arboretum is a free 17-acre garden park with a wide paved walking path, creek and wetland gardens, roses, azaleas, hydrangeas, camellias, hostas, daylilies, native habitat, an accessible suspended Treehouse, Veterans Overlook, Commons Building, restrooms, picnic areas, lawns, and bluebird trail.
