places.hours: The Arboretum is open year-round from sunrise to sunset. The Commons Building, restrooms, guided programs, tours, and events may have narrower schedules.
places.cost: General admission and self-guided walking are free. Programs, tours, rentals, donations, and special events may have separate registration or costs.
places.parking: Use signed public parking near Willowbrook Drive and choose the access closest to the Commons Building, Treehouse, or garden area you want. Do not block nearby residential or service access.
places.restroom: Restrooms are located at the Commons Building. Building access and maintenance may not span every sunrise-to-sunset park hour, so plan accordingly.
places.accessibility: A wide paved path runs through the park, and the Treehouse is described as accessible. Creek edges, lawns, garden beds, wet areas, and individual overlooks can vary in slope and surface.
places.trail: The principal route is a wide paved linear walk through garden collections and along the creek. This is a botanical stroll rather than a rugged hiking trail; allow time for an out-and-back if parking at one end.
places.family: The accessible Treehouse, bluebird boxes, creek, wildlife habitat, sculptures, lawns, and changing flowers offer a calm family visit. Supervise children around water and garden beds.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled, remove waste, and keep pets out of planting beds, buildings, picnic food areas, and sensitive wildlife habitat.
places.picnic: Picnic areas near the Commons Building and open lawns support small gatherings. Keep pathways and garden access clear and verify any group reservation requirements.
places.landmarks: Look for the Commons Building and bluebird metalwork, accessible locust-wood Treehouse near Willowbrook and Sunset, Veterans Overlook, creek, wetland garden, great lawn, flower collections, native grasses, and 18-box Charles Hawks Memorial Bluebird Trail.
places.closures: Flooding, storms, garden maintenance, special events, creek conditions, and building work may affect sections. Plant displays are seasonal even though the park is open year-round.

places.name: Lake Mackintosh Park and Marina
places.operator: City of Burlington Recreation and Parks
places.address: 2704 Huffman Mill Road, Burlington, NC 27215. Use the staffed marina gate for boat ramps, rental boats, pier and bank fishing, playground, picnic sites, shelter, and lakeside clubhouse.
places.summary: Lake Mackintosh is Burlington's 1,150-acre primary drinking-water reservoir with 61 miles of shoreline, offering staffed boat ramps, seasonal kayak and canoe rentals, rowboats, pier and bank fishing, playground, picnic sites and grills, an open-air shelter, and a rentable lakeside clubhouse.
places.hours: The park is closed every Monday and Tuesday. In 2026 gate hours vary from 8 am-5 pm in winter to 6:30 am-8 pm in peak summer. The park, bank fishing, and rentals end 30 minutes before gate closing; boat launching ends 90 minutes before closing.
places.cost: Bank fishing is $3 for adults and $2 for seniors; private boat launch is $10/$7; kayak, canoe, or SUP launch is $7/$5. Solo kayaks and rowboats are $25, tandem kayaks or canoes $30, with separate season passes and rental fees.
places.parking: Enter through the marina gate and park in signed areas for boat trailers, fishing, playground, picnic, shelter, or clubhouse use. Do not use trailer spaces for ordinary park visits during busy boating periods.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available in the developed marina and park area during operating hours. They are unavailable when the gated facility is closed Monday, Tuesday, overnight, or for weather.
places.accessibility: Developed parking, pier, picnic, and building approaches serve the park, but bank-fishing terrain, docks, water levels, boat transfer, and individual rental craft vary. Contact marina staff for specific assistance.
places.trail: This destination emphasizes shoreline recreation rather than a documented long trail. Walk only in designated park areas and stay out of reservoir buffer or operational zones.
places.family: The playground, picnic sites, lake views, fishing pier, rental boats, and shelter work for families. Swimming, wading, skiing, and personal watercraft are prohibited because this is a drinking-water reservoir.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed in allowed land areas, remove waste, and keep pets away from playgrounds, buildings, docks, rental craft, fishing activity, and protected reservoir edges as posted.
places.picnic: Picnic tables and grills, an open-air rental shelter, and a lakeside clubhouse support groups. Reserve ahead and remember the entire facility follows marina gate days and seasonal hours.
places.landmarks: Key points are the Huffman Mill Road gate, marina office, six boat ramps, rental-craft area, fishing pier and banks, playground, picnic sites, open-air shelter, clubhouse, Greater Alamance Creek, and Little Alamance Creek arms.
places.closures: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Inclement weather can cause early closure, and launch access stops 90 minutes before the gate. Kayak and canoe rentals require water temperature of at least 60°F and combined air-plus-water temperature of at least 120°F.

places.name: Lake Cammack Park and Marina
places.operator: City of Burlington Recreation and Parks
places.address: 4790 Union Ridge Road, Burlington, NC 27217. Enter through the staffed marina gate for boat ramps, accessible fishing pier, bank fishing, playground, two-mile hiking trail, Civitan shelter and building, and Camp Green Leaves area.
places.summary: Lake Cammack is an 800-plus-acre secondary drinking-water reservoir with more than 50 miles of shoreline, offering boating and paddling, bank and accessible-pier fishing, a playground, a two-mile hiking trail, picnic shelter, rentable Civitan Building, wildlife viewing, and seasonal recreation.
places.hours: The lake is closed every Wednesday and Thursday. In 2026 hours vary seasonally from 8 am-5 pm in winter to 6:30 am-8 pm in summer; January and December are open Saturday-Tuesday only. Park and trail access ends 30 minutes before the gate, and launching ends 90 minutes before closing.
places.cost: Private boat launch is $10 for adults and $7 for seniors; kayak, canoe, or SUP launch is $7/$5; bank or pier fishing is $3/$2. Season passes, shelter, Civitan Building, pool rentals, and programs have separate fees.
places.parking: Use signed marina parking and preserve boat-trailer spaces for launch users. The playground, fishing, trail, shelter, building, and camp areas are spread around the developed property.
places.restroom: Restrooms serve the marina and developed rental or recreation area during operating hours. The gated property is unavailable on weekly closure days and overnight.
places.accessibility: The fishing pier is identified as accessible, with developed parking and building approaches. The natural hiking trail, bank-fishing areas, docks, water levels, and boat-transfer conditions vary.
places.trail: A two-mile hiking trail offers forest, shoreline, deer, and bird-viewing opportunities. Bikes are not permitted on pedestrian walkways; finish before the trail closes 30 minutes ahead of the gate.
places.family: The playground, accessible fishing pier, trail, picnic facilities, wildlife, and lake views support family visits. Swimming and wading are prohibited because Lake Cammack is a public drinking-water reserve.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed where allowed, remove waste, and keep pets away from playgrounds, buildings, Camp Green Leaves activities, docks, fishing lines, and protected water-supply areas.
places.picnic: The Civitan open-air shelter and Civitan Building are rentable, with additional picnic options. Reservations do not override marina closure days, gate hours, events, or weather shutdowns.
places.landmarks: Orientation points include the Union Ridge Road gate, marina office, boat ramps, accessible fishing pier, bank-fishing areas, playground, two-mile trail, Civitan shelter, Civitan Building, Camp Green Leaves, and reservoir shoreline.
places.closures: Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays, with more limited Saturday-Tuesday operation in January and December. Weather may close the lake early, launches stop 90 minutes before closing, and special events such as triathlons can delay public opening.

places.name: Liberty Park
places.operator: Town of Mooresville Parks & Recreation
places.sourceLabel: Town of Mooresville Park & Facility Finder
places.address: 217 E Iredell Avenue, Mooresville, NC 28115. The park is immediately east of downtown; use the signed public entrance and parking serving the playground, splash pad, amphitheater, shelter, basketball court, and greenway connection.
places.summary: Liberty Park is Mooresville's rebuilt downtown family and event park, with a three-tier playground, interactive splash pad, covered basketball court, amphitheater, reservable picnic shelter, restrooms, concession stand, walking trail, greenway connection, and the historic park bell.
places.hours: The Town's current facility finder lists the basketball courts from sunrise to 10 p.m. Splash-pad, concession, restroom, event, and programmed-area schedules may be narrower; verify seasonal water-play and event details before visiting.
places.cost: General park, playground, trail, lawn, and basketball access is free. Programs, concerts, shelter reservations, concessions, and special events may have separate registration or charges.
places.parking: Use signed public parking at or near 217 E Iredell Avenue and arrive early for concerts, festivals, and splash-pad weather. Downtown event traffic or reserved spaces can change the easiest approach.
places.restroom: Permanent restrooms are part of the rebuilt park near its main family and event facilities. Their availability may follow maintenance, splash-pad, or event schedules rather than the full court hours.
places.accessibility: The rebuilt downtown park uses developed paths linking major facilities. The three-tier playground, wet splash-pad pavement, event crowds, and sloped connections deserve extra planning for mobility needs; use the closest signed accessible parking and current marked route.
places.trail: A developed walking route and greenway connection to Center Avenue link the park with downtown. This is a compact urban walk rather than a backcountry trail, with hard surfaces around the playground, splash pad, court, shelter, and amphitheater.
places.family: Families can use the three-tier playground, interactive splash pad, covered basketball court, walking paths, picnic shelter, and lawns. Confirm that the splash pad is operating before promising water play and bring a change of clothes and water shoes.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled, remove waste, and keep them out of the playground, active splash pad, court, restroom, concession, and crowded event areas. Liberty Park does not have a designated dog park.
places.picnic: A reservable picnic shelter, concession area, and lawns support meals and gatherings. Reserve the shelter for guaranteed group use and check event rules before bringing equipment or setting up on busy dates.
places.landmarks: Look for the three-tier playground, interactive splash pad, covered basketball court, amphitheater, picnic shelter, concession and restroom building, Center Avenue greenway connection, and Liberty Park bell.
places.closures: Splash-pad operation is seasonal and weather-dependent. Concerts, festivals, rentals, maintenance, and wet or freezing conditions can close or restrict individual facilities while other parts of the park remain available.

places.name: Mazeppa Park
places.operator: Town of Mooresville Parks & Recreation
places.sourceLabel: Town of Mooresville Park & Facility Finder
places.address: 645 Mazeppa Road, Mooresville, NC 28115. This large sports and trail campus is north of downtown near the Motorplex; follow internal signs for the correct field, shelter, playground, or mountain-bike access.
places.summary: Mazeppa Park is a 162.8-acre community sports and nature park with baseball and softball fields, multipurpose fields, playgrounds, reservable and open picnic shelters, restrooms, concessions, a walking route, mountain-bike trails, natural areas, and Wi-Fi around developed facilities.
places.hours: The general park is open sunrise to sunset. The Town lists lighted fields as closing at 11 p.m. and lighted courts at 10 p.m.; games, reservations, maintenance, and trail conditions can create different access windows.
places.cost: General park, playground, walking, mountain-bike, and open-space access is free. League play, tournaments, programs, concessions, and shelter or field reservations may have separate costs.
places.parking: Enter at 645 Mazeppa Road and use the lot nearest your assigned field, playground, shelter, or trail access. The 162.8-acre campus is too large to treat every lot as equally convenient, and tournaments can fill parking quickly.
places.restroom: Restrooms and a concession area serve the developed sports complex. Availability can follow games, staffing, maintenance, or seasonal schedules, so do not assume every building remains open for all trail or park hours.
places.accessibility: Developed parking and paths serve the primary fields, playground, shelters, concessions, and restrooms. Natural terrain and mountain-bike trails are not equivalent to paved accessible routes; confirm the closest lot and surface for a specific destination.
places.trail: The park includes a walking route and natural-surface mountain-bike trails. Trail surfaces, roots, mud, grades, and directional rules can vary; avoid riding when wet and follow current signs so fields and natural areas are protected.
places.family: Playgrounds, ballfields, open space, shelters, walking, and youth sports make Mazeppa useful for families. Because destinations are spread out, identify the correct field or activity before arrival and bring sun, water, and weather protection.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and controlled, remove waste, and keep them off active fields, playgrounds, concession and restroom areas, and bike-trail travel lines. Mazeppa Park does not have a designated dog park.
places.picnic: The park has both reservable and non-reservable picnic shelters. Reserve ahead for teams or groups, name the exact shelter in invitations, and avoid blocking field circulation or trail access.
places.landmarks: Major orientation points are the baseball and softball complex, multipurpose fields, playgrounds, reservable and open shelters, concession and restroom area, walking route, mountain-bike trail system, and surrounding natural acreage.
places.closures: Tournaments, league reservations, field recovery, storms, wet trails, maintenance, and nearby large events can affect parking or individual facilities. Lighted play may continue after the general sunrise-to-sunset window only when scheduled.

places.name: Cornelius Road Park
places.operator: Town of Mooresville Parks & Recreation
places.sourceLabel: Town of Mooresville Park & Facility Finder
places.address: 247 Cornelius Road, Mooresville, NC 28117. Use the signed park entrance and then follow internal wayfinding for the turf fields, baseball fields, playground, dog park, courts, disc golf, shelters, or concessions.
places.summary: Cornelius Road Park is a large multi-sport campus with three artificial-turf soccer and lacrosse fields, baseball fields, playground, Officer Jordan H. Sheldon Memorial Dog Park, pickleball and tennis courts, disc golf, walking paths, reservable shelter, restrooms, concessions, and extensive parking.
places.hours: The current Town facility finder lists the general park from sunrise to sunset, lighted fields until 11 p.m., and lighted courts until 10 p.m. Scheduled games, reservations, dog-park maintenance, and facility work may alter access.
places.cost: General park, playground, walking, dog-park, court, and disc-golf access is free unless a posted program or reservation says otherwise. League play, tournaments, rentals, concessions, and organized programs may charge separately.
places.parking: Enter from Cornelius Road and choose the lot closest to your destination. The expanded campus added 288 parking spaces and a turn lane, but tournaments can still create heavy arrival traffic; know your assigned field before entering.
places.restroom: Restrooms serve the developed sports campus, including facilities added with the recent expansion. Hours may follow field use, staffing, or maintenance rather than every sunrise-to-sunset park period.
places.accessibility: Large paved parking areas and developed routes serve major fields, courts, playground, shelters, dog park, concessions, and restrooms. Distances between zones can be substantial; use the closest signed accessible spaces and confirm a specific field route when needed.
places.trail: Walking paths connect developed areas, while the disc-golf course and field edges can involve grass or uneven ground. This is primarily a sports campus rather than a long hiking destination; stay clear of active play and flying discs.
places.family: Families can use the playground, walking paths, baseball and turf fields, courts, disc golf, shelter, little library, and dog park. Tournament crowds and the park's size make advance field and parking orientation especially useful.
places.dogs: The Officer Jordan H. Sheldon Memorial Dog Park provides fenced off-leash green space, water stations, seating, and agility equipment. Leash dogs outside the enclosure and keep them away from playgrounds, fields, courts, concessions, and restrooms.
places.picnic: A reservable shelter and developed gathering areas support team meals and family groups. Reserve for guaranteed use, identify the shelter and nearest lot clearly, and follow posted rules for vendors or event setups.
places.landmarks: Key areas include the three artificial-turf soccer and lacrosse fields, baseball fields, Officer Jordan H. Sheldon Memorial Dog Park, playground, pickleball and tennis courts, disc-golf course, concession and restroom facilities, shelter, and little library.
places.closures: Games, tournaments, field reservations, turf or lighting maintenance, dog-park work, and severe weather can restrict individual areas. The current Town finder indicates the park is operating, superseding the older 2024 construction notice that projected a summer 2025 reopening.

places.name: E. Carroll Joyner Park
places.operator: Town of Wake Forest Parks, Recreation & Cultural Resources
places.address: 701 Harris Road, Wake Forest, NC 27587. Follow park signs for the restored farm buildings, gardens, amphitheater, community center, trails, fishing area, and event parking.
places.summary: E. Carroll Joyner Park is Wake Forest's 117-acre signature park, with restored farm buildings, a pecan grove, 1,000-lawn-seat amphitheater, Walker and Performance gardens, a 2,000-foot stone ribbon wall, three miles of paved trails, fishing, grills, and a community center.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open daily from dawn to dusk. The community center, rentals, performances, fishing, programs, and special events may follow separate schedules.
places.cost: General park, trail, garden, historic-area, and open-space access is free. Community-center programs, amphitheater or garden rentals, classes, and special events may require registration or fees.
places.parking: Use the signed lots at 701 Harris Road and choose the area nearest your destination. Major concerts and community events use special parking and traffic plans, so follow current Town instructions rather than assuming the ordinary lot pattern.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available in developed park and community-center areas during their operating periods. Building access and event facilities may not remain open for every dawn-to-dusk trail visit.
places.accessibility: Paved routes serve the community center and major park destinations, and the three-mile trail system supports wheeled mobility on developed surfaces. Lawns, gardens, fishing edges, historic structures, and crowded events can present different grades or surfaces.
places.trail: The park has about three miles of paved trails suitable for walking, biking, and in-line skating. Use posted etiquette, control speed around walkers and events, and allow extra distance when looping among the gardens, farm structures, and community center.
places.family: Families can explore the paved trails, historic farm buildings, gardens, pecan grove, stone ribbon wall, fishing area, StoryWalk and TRACK Trail activities, concerts, and open lawns. This park does not center on a conventional playground.
places.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed, and visitors must remove waste; receptacles and bags are provided. Keep pets out of buildings, sensitive gardens, crowded performance areas, and places where posted event rules prohibit them.
places.picnic: The park provides charcoal grills and rentable open spaces, gardens, and event facilities. Personal grills are prohibited, so use only Town-provided grills and reserve spaces when planning a group gathering.
places.landmarks: Look for the restored Walker farm buildings, pecan grove, 1,000-seat lawn amphitheater, Walker Garden, Performance Garden, 2,000-foot stone ribbon wall, paved trail loops, community center, and fishing water.
places.closures: Concerts, rentals, large events, construction, storms, fishing conditions, and maintenance can affect individual areas. A separate skate park and pump track project is still in design and should not be represented as currently available.

places.name: Holding Park
places.operator: Town of Wake Forest Parks, Recreation & Cultural Resources
places.address: 133 W Owen Avenue, Wake Forest, NC 27587. The compact five-acre campus includes the inclusive playground, Holding Park Aquatic Center, Wake Forest Community House, basketball court, picnic area, rain garden, and historic pool structures.
places.summary: Holding Park is a compact historic family campus with a fully ramped inclusive playground, rubber play surface and sensory equipment, seasonal aquatic center, basketball court, picnic tables, Town charcoal grills, rain and pollinator gardens, and the WPA-era Wake Forest Community House.
places.hours: The park and inclusive playground are open daily from dawn to dusk. In 2026 the aquatic center operates seasonally from May 23 through Labor Day with separate session hours; the Community House follows rental and program schedules.
places.cost: General park, playground, basketball, garden, and picnic access is free. For 2026, aquatic admission ranges from $1-$5 for Wake Forest residents and $2-$7 for nonresidents depending on age; rentals and programs cost separately.
places.parking: A small gravel lot sits across from the Community House, with some legal on-street parking nearby. The campus is compact and parking fills quickly during swim sessions and events; use only signed spaces and follow temporary Town parking plans.
places.restroom: Restrooms are available at the aquatic center and inside the Community House during their operating periods. Do not assume either building is open for every dawn-to-dusk playground visit.
places.accessibility: The fenced inclusive playground has wheelchair-friendly entrances and benches, enhanced walkways, smooth rubber surfacing, integrated ramps, sensory equipment, and zero-entry play elements. Confirm aquatic transfer and changing-room details separately.
places.trail: Holding Park is a compact five-acre destination rather than a trail park. Developed walkways link the playground, aquatic center, Community House, court, picnic area, and gardens; nearby sidewalks connect toward downtown.
places.family: The inclusive playground supports varied mobility, sensory, cognitive, and social needs with ramps, swings, spinners, slides, musical play, calm space, and group equipment. The seasonal aquatic center adds a six-lane pool, two slides, and children's water play.
places.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed and waste must be removed; bags and receptacles are provided. Keep pets out of the fenced playground, aquatic center, Community House, basketball court, and food or crowded gathering areas.
places.picnic: Picnic tables and Town charcoal grills are available. Personal gas or charcoal grills are prohibited, and Community House or organized-event use requires a reservation.
places.landmarks: Key features are the inclusive playground, Holding Park Aquatic Center, Wake Forest Community House, basketball court, rain garden, pollinator garden, and the large stone retaining wall and stairs that survive from the original 1940s diving platform.
places.closures: The aquatic center is seasonal and weather-sensitive, with capacity and session rules. Swim meets, private events, Community House rentals, maintenance, storms, and wet or icy playground surfaces can affect parts of the campus while the park remains open.

places.name: J.B. Flaherty Park
places.operator: Town of Wake Forest Parks, Recreation & Cultural Resources
places.address: 1100 N White Street, Wake Forest, NC 27587. The community center uses 1226 N White Street; follow internal signs for fields, playground, ponds, courts, fitness court, dog park, shelter, trail, and restrooms.
places.summary: J.B. Flaherty Park is a 100-acre recreation campus with three lighted baseball and softball fields, playground, outdoor fitness court, picnic shelter, two fishing ponds, lighted pickleball and tennis courts, community center, dog park, restrooms, and a quarter-mile paved trail.
places.hours: The outdoor park is open daily from dawn to dusk. The community center is generally open Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-9 p.m., Saturday 8 a.m.-4 p.m., and Sunday 1-5 p.m. March-August only; fields and lighted courts follow schedules and reservations.
places.cost: General outdoor park, playground, trail, fitness court, court, pond-edge, and dog-park access is free when not reserved. Fishing requires the proper license or permit; programs, leagues, rentals, and some indoor activities may charge.
places.parking: Use the N White Street entrance and the lot closest to your assigned field, court, community center, dog park, playground, pond, or shelter. League play and tournaments can create heavy parking demand.
places.restroom: Restrooms serve the developed park and community center. Indoor restrooms follow building hours, while field or event facilities may follow scheduled use and maintenance.
places.accessibility: Developed parking and paved routes connect major facilities, and the quarter-mile asphalt trail links the community center and tennis courts with fields and dog park. Pond banks, grass field edges, and some recreation surfaces vary.
places.trail: A 10-foot-wide paved asphalt trail runs about 0.25 mile through the park, crossing the pond dam and connecting the community center and tennis courts with baseball fields and dog park.
places.family: Families can use the slides and swings, ballfields, paved trail, fishing ponds, courts, picnic shelter, outdoor fitness court, dog park, and community-center programs. Supervise closely around ponds and active sport areas.
places.dogs: Dogs must be leashed in the general park and waste removed. Use the separate Flaherty Dog Park for allowed off-leash activity, and keep pets away from playgrounds, fields, courts, indoor facilities, and fishing lines.
places.picnic: A picnic shelter supports gatherings. Personal gas and charcoal grills are prohibited, so follow the shelter rules and reserve ahead when guaranteed group use matters.
places.landmarks: Orientation points include the community center, three lighted ballfields, playground, Wegmans Outdoor Fitness Court, two ponds and dam crossing, pickleball and tennis courts, picnic shelter, dog park, restrooms, and paved connector trail.
places.closures: League reservations, tournaments, field renovation, court maintenance, pond or dam work, severe weather, and community-center programming can affect individual areas. Check the Town weather and closure notices before organized sports.

places.name: Smith Creek Greenway
places.operator: Town of Wake Forest Parks, Recreation & Cultural Resources
places.address: The southern 1.15-mile segment extends from Burlington Mills Road to the Neuse River Greenway. Official parking is reached through the Neuse network at WRAL Soccer Park, 7700 Perry Creek Road; Horseshoe Nature Preserve, 2900 Horse Shoe Farm Road; or Thornton Road access, 6100 Thornton Road.
places.summary: Smith Creek Greenway's southern segment is a 1.15-mile, 10-foot-wide paved asphalt trail through partly shaded creek and wetland habitat, crossing the Neuse on a 558-foot pedestrian bridge and connecting to the much longer Neuse River Greenway network.
places.hours: The greenway is open dawn to dusk. Start early enough to complete the out-and-back or connected route before dark, since the trail and bridge are not intended as an after-hours corridor.
places.cost: Greenway access is free. Parking, programs, or facilities at connected parks may have their own rules, and riders are responsible for repair, transit, or pickup costs on long one-way trips.
places.parking: The Town directs visitors to WRAL Soccer Park, Horseshoe Nature Preserve, or Thornton Road Greenway access, then to Smith Creek via the Neuse River Greenway. Do not assume Burlington Mills Road provides a full public trailhead lot.
places.restroom: The Town does not list restrooms on the 1.15-mile southern segment. Restroom availability at connected parks or trailheads varies, so use facilities before entering and do not rely on an open building along the route.
places.accessibility: The principal trail is 10-foot-wide paved asphalt and the river crossing is a large pedestrian bridge. Grades, bridge approaches, wet leaves, debris, flooding, and distances to parking can affect access; plan an achievable turnaround.
places.trail: The trail runs 1.15 miles one way from Burlington Mills Road south along Smith Creek to the Neuse River Greenway. It is paved asphalt, 10 feet wide, partly shaded, and can become part of a roughly 33-mile one-way connected route.
places.family: Creek and wetland views, shade, wildlife, and the 558-foot bridge can make a memorable family ride or walk. There is no playground on this segment, and the distance from official parking makes turnaround planning important.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed, under close control, and on the paved trail; remove all waste. Carry water and avoid blocking cyclists or other users on the bridge and narrower approach areas.
places.picnic: There are no documented picnic facilities on the southern segment itself. Use designated picnic areas at connected parks and keep trail shoulders, bridge approaches, wetlands, and private neighborhood access clear.
places.landmarks: The defining features are Smith Creek, aquatic and wetland habitat, partial forest shade, the 558-foot pedestrian bridge over the Neuse River, neighborhood connections near Creek Moss Avenue, and the junction with the Neuse River Greenway.
places.closures: Flooding, storms, sewer or greenway construction, bridge maintenance, and debris can close or narrow the route. Planned northern extensions do not yet make this southern segment continuous with every other Smith Creek section; verify current detours before a long trip.

places.name: Carrier Park
places.operator: Asheville Parks & Recreation
places.address: 220 Amboy Road, Asheville, NC 28806. During recovery, use the east parking lot for the open picnic shelter, wetlands education area, rolling lawn, and French Broad River Greenway access.
places.summary: Carrier Park is a 32-acre French Broad riverfront park built on a former racetrack, normally known for its velodrome, playground, courts, ballfield, lawn bowling, picnic shelter, wetlands, lawn, and greenway; major west-side facilities remain closed during Helene recovery.
places.hours: Normal City park hours are 6 a.m.-10 p.m., but only designated reopened areas may be entered. Temporary fencing and posted recovery restrictions override ordinary hours.
places.cost: Access to reopened park and greenway areas is free. Rentals, leagues, events, and future restored facilities may have separate fees.
places.parking: Use the east parking lot for currently open areas. Do not drive or walk into the closed west side; follow temporary traffic, barrier, and parking signs because recovery work can change circulation.
places.restroom: Portable toilets are located near the open picnic shelter. Do not rely on closed west-side buildings or former restroom locations during recovery.
places.accessibility: The east lot, shelter area, lawn, wetlands area, and open greenway provide the current developed approach, but storm damage, temporary surfaces, barriers, and detours can affect accessibility. Check current City notices before traveling.
places.trail: The French Broad River Greenway through Carrier Park is open, including the connection toward Hominy Creek and Amboy Riverfront Park. Stay on the signed open route and do not cross barriers into damaged park facilities.
places.family: The open east side offers lawn, wetland learning, picnicking, and greenway walking or riding. The west-side playground, velodrome, ballfield, and courts remain closed and should not be promised as available.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and remove waste in open areas. Carrier's former dog-park availability should not be assumed during riverfront recovery; use a currently designated City dog park instead.
places.picnic: The picnic shelter, nearby lawn, and east-side area are open. Confirm reservations and current access before a group event, and keep all setup outside fenced recovery zones.
places.landmarks: The defining features are the former motor-speedway velodrome, French Broad River, greenway, east-side picnic shelter, wetlands education area, rolling lawn, and currently closed west-side recreation complex.
places.closures: Carrier Park is partially open. The east parking lot, picnic shelter, wetlands area, lawn, and greenway are open; the west side, including velodrome, ballfield, playground, and courts, remains closed during Helene recovery.

places.name: French Broad River Park
places.operator: Asheville Parks & Recreation
places.address: 508 Riverview Drive, Asheville, NC 28806. The park is currently closed; do not route visitors through gates or barriers. Use a confirmed open riverfront park or greenway access instead.
places.summary: French Broad River Park is a major riverfront green space normally offering paved paths, river views, mature trees, lawns, gazebo, picnic tables and grills, dog park, parking, restrooms, and greenway access, but it remains closed because of Tropical Storm Helene damage.
places.hours: The posted normal schedule is 6 a.m.-10 p.m., but the park is currently closed. Closure signs and barriers supersede listed operating hours.
places.cost: The park ordinarily has free general access, but no public recreational entry is currently available. Do not pay or park elsewhere expecting to enter through a closed connection.
places.parking: Do not use the Riverview Drive lots as an active park destination while closure remains in effect. Choose an officially open riverfront access and verify the connected greenway segment before leaving.
places.restroom: Park restrooms are unavailable while the site is closed. Use facilities at an open destination before approaching the riverfront network.
places.accessibility: There is no verified public accessible route into the closed park. Recovery design is intended to rebuild a more resilient system, but future concepts are not current visitor facilities.
places.trail: The greenway portion within French Broad River Park and the connection toward Amboy Riverfront Park remain closed. Other French Broad River Greenway sections may be open, so plan from a current City recovery map rather than assuming continuity.
places.family: Do not plan a family visit inside this park while closed. Use an open Asheville park for play, picnicking, dog exercise, and restroom access, and treat riverfront barriers as firm safety limits.
places.dogs: The park's dog area is unavailable during closure. Use a currently open designated dog park and do not bypass barriers to reach former off-leash facilities.
places.picnic: The gazebo, tables, grills, and lawns are unavailable while the park is closed. Move gatherings to a confirmed open reservable site.
places.landmarks: When restored, the park is known for the French Broad River, mature tree canopy, broad lawns, gazebo, dog park, paved paths, and greenway. These features should not be interpreted as currently accessible.
places.closures: The entire park remains closed due to Helene damage, and riverfront rebuilding is still in design. Check the City recovery page for any phased reopening before visiting.

places.name: Richmond Hill Park
places.operator: Asheville Parks & Recreation
places.address: 300 Richmond Hill Drive, Asheville, NC 28806. Enter through the signed park drive and use the main lot for currently open disc golf, trails, picnic shelter, restrooms, lawn, and bike-skills access.
places.summary: Richmond Hill Park is a wooded West Asheville destination with an 18-hole disc golf course, hiking and mountain-bike trails, bike-skills area, picnic shelter, winterized restrooms, lawn, drinking fountain, and natural terrain; it is only partially reopened after Helene.
places.hours: Open areas follow normal park hours of 6 a.m.-10 p.m. Temporary trail closures, fencing, and storm-recovery signs override the general schedule.
places.cost: General park, disc-golf, trail, bike-skills, lawn, and picnic access is free. Organized events or shelter use may require reservations or fees.
places.parking: Use the main lot at 300 Richmond Hill Drive and follow current internal signs. Park only in designated spaces and avoid staging on recovery access routes.
places.restroom: Winterized restrooms and a drinking fountain with bottle filler and pet dish serve the developed picnic area. Availability can be affected by maintenance or recovery work.
places.accessibility: Accessible walkways connect parking with the newer shelter, restroom, lawn, and site furnishings. Natural-surface hiking, biking, disc-golf terrain, roots, grades, and storm damage vary substantially.
places.trail: Some hiking and mountain-bike trails have reopened, but conditions changed after the storm. Follow temporary signs, avoid closed or wet routes, and choose difficulty appropriate to the rider; the bike-skills trail includes beginner through advanced options.
places.family: Families can use the open lawn, shelter, disc golf, selected trails, and bike-skills features, including options intended for young balance-bike riders. Confirm trail status and bring helmets, water, and terrain-appropriate footwear.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and remove waste. The drinking fountain includes a pet dish, but dogs should remain clear of disc-flight paths, cyclists, restrooms, and closed recovery areas.
places.picnic: A covered community shelter and expanded green space support picnics. Reserve when needed and respect any temporary limits around construction or trail rebuilding.
places.landmarks: Look for the 18-hole disc-golf course, hole-one tee, covered shelter, winterized restroom, expanded lawn, bottle-filler fountain, accessible walkways, wooded trail network, and bike-skills area.
places.closures: The park is partially reopened. Disc golf is fully open and selected trails are open, but hazards remain; obey every temporary sign, fence, and closure while rebuilding continues.

places.name: Pack Square Park
places.operator: Asheville Parks & Recreation
places.address: 80 Court Plaza, Asheville, NC 28801. This downtown civic park spans Pack Square and City-County Plaza; approach on foot from nearby streets, transit stops, or a signed downtown garage.
places.summary: Pack Square Park is Asheville's downtown front yard, with paved walks, terraces, benches, lawns, performance spaces, restrooms, the free seasonal Splasheville play fountain, public art, Urban Trail stations, monuments, native landscaping, and frequent events.
places.hours: The park is open daily from 6 a.m.-10 p.m. Splasheville, restrooms, food trucks, performances, and events operate on narrower seasonal or programmed schedules.
places.cost: General park and seasonal Splasheville access are free. Parking, food, ticketed events, rentals, and permitted private activities may cost separately.
places.parking: There is no dedicated park lot. Use a signed City garage or legal downtown space, check current garage conditions and event closures, or arrive by transit or on foot.
places.restroom: Public restrooms are provided in the park, but hours can be shorter than the full 6 a.m.-10 p.m. park day and may change during maintenance or events.
places.accessibility: The civic park has paved walking paths, terraces, and wheelchair-accessible routes. Event fencing, crowds, wet splash-pad pavement, slopes between plazas, and temporary installations can alter the easiest route.
places.trail: This is a compact paved downtown walking environment rather than a hiking trail. It connects directly with Asheville's Urban Trail, public art, civic buildings, shops, and downtown sidewalks.
places.family: Splasheville offers free seasonal water play, while lawns, public art, Urban Trail stations, performances, and events support family visits. Confirm fountain operation and bring water shoes and dry clothes.
places.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and remove waste. Keep pets out of active splash water, restrooms, food-service areas, dense event crowds, and any space restricted by event rules.
places.picnic: Benches, terraces, and lawns support casual meals, and seasonal food trucks may visit. Tents, inflatables, organized gatherings, and recurring use can require a permit.
places.landmarks: Key sights include Splasheville, Pack Square and City-County Plaza, performance areas, 11 City public-art works including seven Urban Trail stations, courthouse monuments, native plantings, and a surviving downtown phone booth.
places.closures: Splasheville is seasonal and can close for maintenance, weather, or water-quality needs. Festivals, demonstrations, permitted events, construction, and downtown street closures can change access without closing the entire park.

places.name: Western North Carolina Nature Center
places.operator: City of Asheville and Friends of the WNC Nature Center
places.address: 75 Gashes Creek Road, Asheville, NC 28805. Because the former bridge route was lost to Helene, approach via Azalea Road, continue to the roundabout, cross the signal-controlled one-way metal bridge, then turn left onto Gashes Creek Road.
places.summary: The WNC Nature Center is a 42-acre wildlife park focused on Southern Appalachian species, with outdoor habitat trails and more than 60 species including black bears, cougars, wolves, otters, red pandas, reptiles, amphibians, and birds, plus daily activities and education programs.
places.hours: Open seven days a week from 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m., with last admission at 3:30 p.m. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, and New Year's Day; special events use separate hours.
places.cost: Current admission is $16.95 adults and youth 13-15, $15.95 seniors 65+, $12.95 children 3-12, and free for ages two and under, plus tax. Asheville residents receive lower rates, and active-duty or retired military enter free with ID.
places.parking: Use the on-site lots after the temporary metal-bridge approach. On busy days follow signs to overflow parking at John B. Lewis Soccer Complex; the ticket office is cashless.
places.restroom: Visitor restrooms are available within the developed Nature Center during operating hours. Use the entrance-area facilities before longer outdoor habitat loops when needed.
places.accessibility: The center publishes dedicated accessibility guidance, but its outdoor campus includes hills and varied distances. Review the current accessibility page or contact staff for mobility, sensory, service-animal, stroller, or restroom needs before arrival.
places.trail: Outdoor walking routes connect animal habitats across the 42-acre hillside campus. Expect at least a mile for many visits, with grades and weather exposure; special behind-the-scenes programs can explicitly require a mile of walking and steep hills.
places.family: Children can see native and regional wildlife, attend daily activities, and learn about habitats and animal care. Guests under 16 must be accompanied by an adult, and children must be supervised at all times.
places.dogs: Pets are not permitted inside the wildlife center. Contact the center in advance about service-animal procedures because proximity to animal habitats may require specific routing or accommodations.
places.picnic: Use only designated visitor areas and follow posted food rules; do not feed animals or bring food into restricted habitat zones. Group visits and programs require advance planning.
places.landmarks: Popular habitats feature black bears, cougars, red and gray wolves, river otters, red pandas, farm animals, reptiles, amphibians, and native birds, with mountain landscaping and educational exhibits throughout the route.
places.closures: Animal availability, severe weather, habitat work, special events, and the temporary post-Helene access route can affect a visit. Tickets are not refunded or rain-checked solely for animal availability or weather, so check conditions first.
